title: Pre-registered CCA transfer of an EMG decoder between two monkeys failed (FALCON M1). Post-hoc CCA regularisation brought transfer near the threshold, mostly with condition-independent signal
abstract: Question: can a shared low-dimensional M1 latent structure transfer an EMG decoder between two monkeys that do the same reach-to-grasp task, with no target EMG used for training? Data: FALCON M1 (DANDI 000941, 001209), monkeys L and X, 24 location-object conditions, 64 multi-unit M1 channels and the same 16 muscles. Pre-registered test (SHA-256 recorded before any cross-animal fit): 10-D PCA latents, CCA alignment of condition-averaged trajectories (Safaie et al. 2023), and a ridge decoder. The metric was held-out 5-fold R² on the target. The prediction was that the cross/within R² ratio is at least 0.5 in both directions, over 9 held-out session pairs per direction. Result: the prediction failed. With the pre-registered, essentially unregularised CCA (ridge 1e-6), the mean ratio was -0.45 for L to X (95% trial-bootstrap CI -0.88 to -0.23; pair range -1.44 to 0.15) and 0.27 for X to L (CI 0.24 to 0.29; range 0.12 to 0.35). No pair reached 0.5. Post hoc, the size of this failure depends on the CCA regularisation. Unregularised whitening amplifies single-trial noise in the poorly aligned canonical dimensions. With a target-side ridge chosen on the discovery pair only (lambda = 3), the ratios were 0.50 (L to X; 5/9 pairs at or above 0.5) and 0.47 (X to L; 0/9). No lambda in the grid reached 0.5 in both directions. The scale-free r² ratios were 0.62 and 0.59. However, a template of the source animal's mean EMG time course around movement onset uses no neural data and gave R² 0.23 and 0.17, against 0.28 and 0.27 for regularised transfer. Wrong condition matching cost only 0.01 to 0.03 R². So the transferred signal is mostly condition-independent. At equal numbers of labelled target trials, a within-animal decoder beat transfer from 24 trials up. Limitations: one pair of animals, sessions about one week apart, and the regularisation analysis is post hoc. The result applies to EMG with linear CCA transfer.

display.caption: Held-out R² on target EMG for 18 directed session pairs (dots; bars = direction means). Left: pre-registered pipeline (unregularised CCA) and its controls. Middle (post hoc): CCA with target-side ridge lambda = 3 chosen on the discovery pair. Right: baselines without neural data, including the condition-independent grand-mean EMG templates. Values below -1 are clipped.

Post hoc. Left: held-out cross/within ratio (solid: R²; dashed: scale-free r²; band: range over 9 pairs) against the target-side CCA ridge lambda. Lambda = 0 is the pre-registered pipeline. Right: single-trial SD of target canonical variables relative to the source, for lambda = 0 and lambda = 3.

Held-out R² against the number n of target training trials, with the same trial subsets for all curves: within-animal decoder on n labelled trials; transfer with PCA and CCA on n trials (no target EMG) for lambda = 0 and lambda = 3; transfer (lambda = 3) plus a 16x16 output map, with alignment and map both fit on the same n labelled trials.
